proposals.before: Then Grand Agriculture Chen calculated money usage; taxes and levies were already exhausted and insufficient to support war troops.
proposals.after: Then the Grand Minister of Agriculture presented the stored money for current expenditures; taxes and levies were already exhausted and insufficient to support the troops.
proposals.reason: 陳 is the verb “to present/set forth,” not a personal name Chen; the literal invents an official named Chen.

proposals.before: The ladder had seventeen purchasable grades with very high aggregate valuation.
proposals.after: Each grade cost 170,000, totaling over 300,000 in gold.
proposals.reason: 級十七萬 means a price of 170,000 per grade, not “seventeen grades.”

proposals.before: Its 17 levels were priced in total at over three hundred thousand jin of gold.
proposals.after: Each grade was 170,000, totaling over three hundred thousand in gold.

proposals.before: Consequently most merchant households above middling means were ruined; the people took to rich food and fine clothes and no longer pursued storing wealth through farming, while because of revenues from salt, iron, and the min-money policy, government expenditures were somewhat easier to meet.
proposals.after: Consequently most merchant households above middling means were ruined; the people took to rich food and fine clothes and no longer pursued storing wealth through farming, while because of revenues from salt, iron, and the declaration-money levy, government expenditures were somewhat easier to meet.
proposals.reason: 嬢錢 is the declaration/min-money property levy, not a vague “min-money policy”; the phrasing obscures the fiscal measure named in the Chinese.

proposals.before: From the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, when the Three Offices first cast wuzhu coins, to the Zhong era of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping, more than 2.8 trillion coins were minted, it is said.
proposals.after: From the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, when the Three Offices first cast wuzhu coins, to the middle of Yuanshi under Emperor Ping, more than 2.8 trillion coins were minted, it is said.
proposals.reason: Chinese 元始中 means during/in the middle of Yuanshi, not a reign name 'Zhong era of Yuanshi'.

proposals.before: With battle deaths, border captures by surrounding tribes, criminal convictions, famine, epidemic, and cannibalism, by the time Mang had not yet been executed the empire's households had already been reduced by half.
proposals.after: With battle deaths, captures by the Four Barbarians along the borders, criminal convictions, famine, epidemic, and cannibalism, even before Mang had been executed the empire's households and population had already been reduced by half.
proposals.reason: 及莽未誅 means even before Mang was executed; the literal's 'by the time Mang had not yet been executed' reverses the temporal sense.

decisions.after: A bolt of cloth was two chi two cun wide and four zhang long.
decisions.reason: 布帛廣二尺二寸為幅，長四丈為匹 gives the standard width and length of a bolt. The worker correctly restored the measures but confused 幅, the standard width, with 匹, the bolt.

decisions.after: The Grand Minister of Agriculture then reported that the treasury reserves had been consumed by current expenses; taxes and levies were exhausted and no longer sufficient to support the troops.
decisions.reason: In 大司農陳臧錢經用, 陳 is the verb 'to report,' not a surname. The clause says that current expenditure had consumed the stored money, not that the official merely presented money for use.

decisions.after: Each successive grade cost 170,000 cash; altogether the ranks were said to be worth more than 300,000 jin of gold.
decisions.reason: 級十七萬 states a price of 170,000 cash per successive grade, not seventeen grades. The revision supplies the monetary unit and preserves the source's puzzling aggregate rather than silently reconciling it.

decisions.after: Each successive grade cost 170,000 cash; altogether the ranks were worth more than 300,000 jin of gold.
decisions.reason: The same 級十七萬 means 170,000 cash per successive grade. Reading it as seventeen levels is wrong, while the source's own aggregate should be retained as transmitted.

decisions.after: Consequently most merchant households above middling means were ruined; the people took to rich food and fine clothes and no longer pursued storing wealth through farming, while revenues from the salt and iron monopolies and the tax on declared merchant capital gave the government somewhat more room to meet its expenses.
decisions.reason: The received term 緡錢 denotes the property tax assessed on merchants' declared capital. 'Declaration-money levy' is opaque English; this wording identifies the fiscal measure plainly.

decisions.after: From the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu, when the Three Offices first cast wuzhu coins, to the middle of the Yuanshi era under Emperor Ping, more than 280 billion coins were cast, it is said.
decisions.reason: 平帝元始中 means during the middle of the Yuanshi era, and 二百八十億萬餘 is conventionally reported as more than 280 billion coins. The proposal fixed the era phrase but retained the translation's tenfold numerical error.

decisions.after: Through deaths in battle, captures by the Four Barbarians along the frontiers, punishment for crimes, famine, epidemic, and cannibalism, the empire had lost half its households and population even before Wang Mang was killed.
decisions.reason: 及莽未誅 means even before Wang Mang was killed. The revision restores 四夷 and 戶口 while giving the accumulated causes and temporal clause natural English syntax.
